vectors.progress: DELIVERED (verdict .agents/roadmap-verdicts/VC-200-001.json, T-DEEPSEEK-49, 2026-10-04): federated cross-node consensus runs on the production supervisor path — durable pinned-electorate quorum commits, sealed and replicated HMAC-signed CommitRecords, term ordering, anti-entropy repair, compaction, leader election, and endorsement-gated membership consensus (vc_200_001_* tests, swarm_gap_durable_quorum_*, member_signing). Delivery history: PARTIAL: UDP LAN discovery, TCP JSON-RPC peer dispatch, and trust-score ranking already worked. Closed the routing gap the code itself flagged ("bloom-filters of peer registries for perfect routing"): peers now exchange a real 256-bit `CapabilityBloom` of their registered tool names during ping/pong, and `rank_peers_for_goal` scores peers by goal/capability overlap instead of trust alone (`src/gawd/amas.rs`). As of 2026-09-22 (EV-2022922-101), added a real quorum-commit primitive: `SusiSupervisor::quorum_majority` (`src/gawd/amas.rs`) checks the shared mission blackboard — which already holds both local agent outputs and dispatched peer-node outputs under `PeerNode_<id>` keys — for a strict majority of independently-produced entries that exact-match after normalization, and commits that value directly (a new `QUORUM_COMMIT` A2A action, distinct from the pre-existing `STATE_CONVERGENCE` rank-leader/LLM-synthesis paths) instead of only ever picking one rank-leader's answer or asking an LLM to reconcile. Remaining gap narrowed (cluster-key membership landed): peers now exchange an HMAC-SHA256-signed ping/pong (`SUSI_PING_SIG`/`SUSI_PONG_SIG`, susi-peer-v1) keyed by a shared 32-byte secret at ~/.susi/cluster.key (0600, `susi_config::cluster_key`); a pong must echo the requester's nonce, so a spoofed or replayed UDP answer can never promote a peer past `PeerAdmission::Discovered`. Verified peers persist in ~/.susi/peers.json and rehydrate as `Explicit` on restart. As of 2026-09-23, the quorum vote tolerates mid-vote churn via a pinned electorate (the Raft configuration-entry concept applied to one consensus round): supervise_mission snapshots the voter set at broadcast — local fleet names + PeerNode_<id> keys for every Explicit peer actually dispatched — and quorum_majority counts only pinned members, thresholding against the electorate's full size rather than the respondents. A peer dying mid-vote now shrinks the response set instead of silently lowering the quorum bar, and a peer admitted after the broadcast can never tilt the count. Commit replication landed (kernel-ABI commit_log module, vendored to all planes): every QUORUM_COMMIT is sealed into a CommitRecord (pinned electorate, tally, quorum threshold, SHA-256 value hash, HMAC-SHA256 signature under cluster.key), appended to ~/.susi/commit_log.jsonl, and pushed to each voting peer via the governed commit_record tool — receivers verify signature + quorum consistency before appending, so forged or below-quorum records fail closed. A coordinator crash mid-round no longer loses the decision, and commit_log exposes the ledger for audit. Leader election + per-coordinator ordering landed: SusiSupervisor::elect_leader is a deterministic bully election over the verified roster (highest trust, node_id tie-break) — every member converges on the same leader without a round-trip, and Discovered/inactive nodes can never lead. CommitRecord carries seq (per-coordinator monotonic, signed) and leader (elected at commit time); the commit_record receiver runs missing_seqs gap detection and surfaces replication gaps in the tool response, and susi commits shows SEQ per row. Anti-entropy repair landed: commit_record receivers that detect a seq gap resolve the coordinator's address through the new gawd.cluster.peers roster topic and pull missing records via commit_log_fetch, verifying each signature before append — lost replication now self-heals, and a peer that can't reach the coordinator surfaces the gap rather than hiding it. Append is now idempotent with equivocation detection: re-delivered records no-op (replication retries can't corrupt the count-based seq assignment), and a different cluster-signed record claiming an already-held (coordinator, seq) slot is refused as equivocation rather than silently ordering both. Term ordering landed: ~/.susi/term.json holds {term, leader}, bumped by claim_leadership on leader transitions and signed into every CommitRecord; commit_record rejects stale-term pushes (Raft's AppendEntries term check), adopts newer terms (step-down rule), and flags same-term leader conflicts — terms gate new writes while anti-entropy still fills old-term history. State-machine replay landed: commit_log::replay() folds the ledger into ClusterState (max term, leader, per-coordinator high-water seqs, anomalies) so any node holding the same records derives the same consensus view, and susi commits audit/replay plus the new `susi os` unified substrate view surface it to operators. What remains vs full Raft/Paxos: log-matching prevLogIndex/term check landed (each CommitRecord signs prev_epoch — its predecessor's epoch — and receivers refuse a divergent link as fork evidence while replay flags residual chain-breaks); Membership-change consensus landed 2026-09-24: roster deltas are committed to the replicated ledger as leader-signed `member_add`/`member_remove`/`member_unban` records (CommitRecord.kind — Raft's config-entry analog, sealed by susi peers add/remove/unban, pushed through the commit_record tool path, and applied to peers.json/peers_banned.json on append since the ledger IS applied state). Every node also gained a stable persisted identity (~/.susi/node_id, wire_node_id()) — previously all members shared the hardcoded susi-daemon-node id, collapsing per-coordinator seq namespaces and making elections non-deterministic; signed pings now carry the real node_id (7-field wire, 6-field back-compat + peers-add legacy fallback). Replay folds membership deltas into ClusterState.roster/banned so identical logs derive identical membership. Leader-proposed membership landed 2026-09-24: privileged records (member deltas, both rekey phases) are only applied when sealed by a coordinator claiming its own leadership (record.leader == record.coordinator) — Raft's leader-proposed configuration-entry rule; non-leader members delegate member_add through the member_propose tool. Ledger compaction landed the same day: commit_log::compact() folds the live ledger into commit_snapshot.json (high-water marks + derived state) and archives pre-snapshot records to commit_log.archive.jsonl, retaining per-coordinator anchor records so sealing/anti-entropy stay snapshot-unaware; replay seeds from the snapshot so compacted and uncompacted views are identical, commit_log_fetch + anti-entropy serve the archive, and below-floor arrivals dedup against it (identical → no-op, divergent → equivocation). Auto-compacts in the scout sweep at >2048 records; susi commits compact is the manual form. What remains vs full Raft/Paxos: no commit-index/apply phase (the ledger IS the applied state — a deliberate simplification, not a gap), and no true joint-consensus for membership transitions: under a shared symmetric key, multi-signatures are cryptographically meaningless (every member signs identically), so Raft's C_old,new safety needs per-member identity (PKI) to mean anything — leader-proposal + term gates bound a stale leader's divergence but cannot fully serialize overlapping config changes. The honest next step toward it was per-member signing keys — now landed (EV: tests/member_signing.rs): every node holds an Ed25519 identity at ~/.susi/node.key (0600); every sealed record carries member_sig (signature over the record HMAC), and a v2 handshake dialect (SUSI_PING_SIG2/PONG_SIG2, tried first with v1 fallback) attests each responder's pubkey so rosters bind member→key on verified pong or committed member_add (member_pubkey, first-write-wins, key_bound_at=record.committed_at). Once bound, intake refuses records from that coordinator without a valid member_sig — a stolen cluster.key can no longer mint records as a bound member; pre-binding history still converges (committed_at < key_bound_at). Residuals documented in ARCHITECTURE.md: the pre-binding window, backdated committed_at, and proposer-attested member_pubkey are bounded but nonzero until binding is itself consensus-checked — the remaining step toward genuine joint consensus. As of 2026-09-24, the identity stack is complete end-to-end: endorsement-gated privileged records (bound-majority Ed25519 endorsements over `susi-endorse-v1:{signature}` — a stolen cluster.key alone can no longer add, remove, or rekey members), subject-signed key-binding attestations (v3 pong carries `bind_sig` over `susi-bind-v1:{node}:{pubkey}`; `member_add` intake refuses a `member_pubkey` without `subject_sig`), sequence floors (`key_bound_seq` closes the backdated-committed_at forgery window), body-bound v2 request signing (`susi-peer-req-v2` binds method:path:ts:nonce:sha256(body) over the exact wire bytes), pairwise confidentiality (X25519 ECDH + ChaCha20-Poly1305 on requests AND responses, fail-closed on downgrade), and persistent replay resistance (FileLock-serialized seen_nonces.jsonl, incremental tail-fold, 50k cap). Operator surfaces: `peers status` cluster-wide term/leader/epoch view with split-brain flags, `peers probe` non-destructive handshake diagnostics, subject-attestation + endorsement markers in `peers list`/`commits show`. State boundedness: every append-only file is now capped (ledger compaction+archive, context_graph 16MiB auto-compact with incremental replay, seen_nonces window+50k, reasoning_experience 4MB tail-cap, receipt_archive 16MB×8 generations, supervisor/service logs single-gen rotation). Hot paths cache by mtime: roster rows, config, cluster.key/node.key/node_id/api_token/term.json — per-request file reads are down to stats. Identity files (cluster.key, node_id) are installed in full by staged hard-link; an empty file from an interrupted first start is regenerated instead of stranding the node in unsigned mode with an ephemeral id. The ban list fails closed everywhere it is consulted: a damaged peers_banned.json refuses admission and is never rewritten by a committed membership change. The verified roster is edited row by row and never rewritten from a damaged read, so one torn file or foreign row cannot erase every member. OPEN GAP (2026-10-01 source review, main 702e1daddfb0): P1: SusiSupervisor logs local commit_log::append failures yet returns QUORUM_COMMIT, uses detached best-effort replication, and launches peer reasoning without awaiting a bounded collection phase. Specify honest commit durability and acknowledgement semantics; refuse committed success when sealing or durable local append fails, and require acknowledgements if replicated durability is promised. Await dispatched peer responses under a bounded deadline and distinguish agreed text from verified correctness. Keep transport/address labels out of canonical vote values and reject errors, nonmembers and stale authority. Tracked by T-CODEXSWARMGAPS-5; closure requires nonzero swarm_gap_durable_quorum_* production-path regression tests and verified mastery, not task coverage alone.

Quota windows (rolling hours, daily, weekly) are tracked with remaining allowance and reset time, so ranking uses the expected marginal cost of the next call plus the scarcity of a nearly-exhausted cap rather than a naive price per token.

Process-local limits recorded in the verdict.
vectors.vector: Billing mode and quota windows enter the cost model

A primary that times out mid-mission fails over and resumes from durable state instead of restarting.

Remaining: mid-mission failover with durable resume (T-124).

vectors.mastery_target: Work a secondary produced is verified to a depth set by its risk, the cost of that verification enters the routing decision, and an unverified delegation is never presented as though the primary had done it. Verification is where a cheap secondary stops being a quality leak: the mission's result is only as good as what the primary checked.
vectors.progress: DELIVERED (T-126): orchestrated delegations are verified to a depth set by the goal's risk — deterministic check for reflex/chat, an independent working model verifier for code/reasoning; the verifier's marginal cost is inside the delegation bound, a goal with no independent checker is never delegated (HeldBack::NoVerifier), a REFUTED result is rescued by the primary and never presented as its own, and the journaled topology names who produced what and who checked it.
vectors.vector: Delegated work is verified proportionally to risk
